explanation: An exponent just counts repeated factors: a^m is m copies of a multiplied together. When you multiply a^m by a^n you simply pool both piles of factors, so the total count is m + n — that is why the exponents ADD instead of multiplying. Slide m and n and watch the boxes (each box is one factor of a); the moving highlight counts them one at a time so you see m + n directly.
bullets: a^m means a multiplied by itself m times (m factors).
Same base: multiply -> ADD the exponents (pool the factors).
a^0 = 1 because zero factors of a leaves the multiplicative identity.
